transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess... I guess what really brings me in today, what started this whole thing, was this incident at work. I work as a personal care aide, you know, and we have these mandatory staff meetings. Usually they are pretty boring, just sitting around listening to the supervisor drone on about protocols and whatever. But this last one, I don't know, I just got really, really worked up. 

They were talking about fall prevention, which is a huge deal in our line of work, obviously, because if a client falls, that is a massive liability and it is terrible for the client's health. So I am sitting there, and suddenly I just felt this intense need to demonstrate exactly how it happens and how to stop it. Like, just talking about it wasn't enough, people needed to see it. So I got up, and I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was grabbing chairs, pulling them into the middle of the floor, waving my arms around to show the exact angles and the momentum of a fall, just really getting into the physical space of it and showing how you have to block them. 

And the thing is, I couldn't seem to stop. My supervisor, my coworkers, they were all looking at me and telling me to sit down, telling me they understood and to please take a seat, but I just kept going. It was like I had to finish the whole routine, every single step, even with folks telling me to sit down. I just couldn't turn it off, you know? And after that, well, my boss pulled me aside and said I needed to come talk to someone, so here I am.
When you were acting out that fall-prevention drill, how were you feeling emotionally? Were you feeling unusually excited, agitated, or like you couldn’t control your energy?

Well, it’s hard to describe exactly, but yeah, I was definitely feeling... I don't know, just so incredibly fired up. It’s like, there are these stretches of time, and this was definitely one of them, where I just feel so bright and energized, like everything is finally lining up perfectly in my head and I understand exactly what needs to be done. The energy just bubbles up, you know? Like I’m running on a totally different frequency than everyone else in the room. I was so excited about the drill, so convinced that I was doing this amazing, helpful thing by showing them the mechanics of it. I felt fantastic, honestly. 

But then, at the same time, when they started telling me to sit down, when my supervisor was trying to interrupt me and slow me down... man, that just completely changed the channel for me. If I'm feeling that good, that dialed in, and someone tries to put the brakes on or questions what I’m doing, I just snap. And I snap way harder than I mean to. It’s like this intense irritation just flares up out of nowhere because they just aren't getting it, they aren't seeing how important and brilliant what I'm doing is. So I guess it was this mix of feeling totally unstoppable and brilliant, but also getting incredibly agitated and short-tempered the second anyone tried to get in my way or tell me to stop. I just couldn't stand being interrupted when I was on that kind of a roll.

Have you had any other times in your life when you felt unusually energetic, excited, or on top of the world for days at a time, where your mood was really different from usual and maybe other people noticed something was off?

Oh, absolutely. Yeah, it's not just the one time at the staff meeting. This happens... well, it happens in these waves, I guess you could call them. There are these days, sometimes a whole string of days, where I just wake up and I am absolutely buzzing. It's like my battery is charged to 200 percent. On those high-energy days, man, I get so much done. It’s incredible. I’ll wake up at, I don't know, four in the morning, and I won't even be tired. I'll just jump right out of bed and start tackling projects that have been sitting around for months. 

Like, a few weeks ago, I had one of these stretches, and I completely emptied out every single closet in my apartment. I pulled everything out, sorted it all by season and color, folded it perfectly, and put it all back. And then, because I still had so much energy and it was only like 6:00 AM, I started completely rewriting all the care checklists for my clients at work. I had these brilliant ideas for how to streamline their morning routines, how to make the meal prep more efficient, and I was just writing page after page of these new protocols. 

And then, I got this idea that my church really needed a health fair. Like, a full-on community event with blood pressure screenings and nutrition booths. So I started planning the whole thing right there at my kitchen table. I was sketching out the floor plan for the fellowship hall, making lists of which nurses and doctors in the congregation I needed to recruit. And because it all felt so urgent, like it had to happen right then, I started calling people. I was calling folks from church, calling my coworkers about the new checklists, and it was barely past dawn. People were answering the phone all groggy, like, "Do you know what time it is?" but I just couldn't wait. The ideas were coming so fast, and I just had to act on them immediately. It’s like I have this incredible drive to fix everything and organize everything all at once, and I just can't slow down until it's all done.

Have there been times when you felt this way for several days in a row — not just for a few hours — where your mood was really elevated or you were unusually irritable, and you were also more active or energetic than usual?

Oh, yeah, absolutely. It's never just a few hours. When this hits, when that switch flips and I'm suddenly running on all cylinders, it lasts for days. I mean, days and days in a row. It's like I get on this high-speed train and I can't get off until it finally runs out of track. 

And you know, now that I really sit down and think about it, looking back over the calendar... this hasn't just been a recent thing, either. These stretches—where I'm just way too energized, where I'm barely sleeping at all, like maybe an hour or two a night and feeling totally fine, and where I'm just pushing these massive, grand plans on everyone around me—they've been coming and going for a while now. I'd say it's been happening for about eleven months. 

Yeah, almost a full year of this cycle. It started around the end of last summer, I remember because I had this whole grand idea to completely landscape my apartment complex's courtyard by myself over a weekend, which didn't go over well with the landlord, let me tell you. But yeah, for about eleven months now, I'll have these periods lasting several days, sometimes a whole week, where I'm just buzzing. I'm up all night, I'm planning, I'm organizing, I'm calling people, and if anyone tries to slow me down or tell me I'm doing too much, I just get so incredibly irritated with them. It's like they're walking in slow motion and I'm sprinting, and I just can't stand it. So yes, it definitely lasts for days at a time, and this whole pattern has been going on for nearly a year.

latest_inference.note: The patient has described a pattern of recurrent manic episodes lasting several days, with elevated mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and irritability when interrupted. These symptoms have been occurring for nearly 11 months, supporting a diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder, Current Episode Manic, Moderate or Severe with Mood Congruent Psychotic Features (F31.13). Other codes in the F31.1 series were ruled out based on the severity, duration, and clinical features of the episodes.
